primary_claim: Declining breeding populations in two Pygoscelis species and two Antarctic monitoring systems lost effective breeding-component number faster than expected under proportional thinning plus frozen count-error models.
secondary_descriptive_claim: Palmer concentration involved dominance turnover, whereas both Signy populations retained and strengthened the initially dominant breeding component.
freeze_rules: No new ecological endpoint may be added before initial submission.
No new concentration metric, threshold, time window, error model or rescue analysis may be added.
Only copyediting, reference completion, journal formatting, author metadata, acknowledgments, contribution statements, conflict statements, open-research wording and archival links may change.
Any scientifically substantive post-freeze change requires a new manuscript version and an explicit provenance note.
